raw_case_text:
A 49-year-old man living in Sao Paulo, Brazil, and working as a marble and tile setter in the construction industry, was admitted to the hospital with acute, diffuse abdominal pain, arterial hypotension, and jaundice. The patient reported exposure to floodwater and ingestion of contaminated water 10 days prior to symptom onset. On admission, an abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan revealed pneumoperitoneum near the gallbladder and bile ducts. An exploratory laparotomy with cholecystectomy was performed, but no gastroduodenal perforation was observed. The patient remained in the intensive care unit (ICU), where he developed jaundice, acute renal failure requiring hemodialysis, and alveolar hemorrhage necessitating orotracheal intubation. Laboratory investigation confirmed leptospirosis by two consecutive serological tests: ELISA-IgM and a microscopic agglutination test for the serovar Cynopteri, with a titer of 1/800. He was treated with ceftriaxone for 14 days, leading to clinical and laboratory improvement.
After two weeks hospitalized, the patient experienced multiple episodes of severe enterorrhagia and required a massive transfusion of 10 units of red blood cells. Due to ongoing bleeding, a total colectomy with terminal ileostomy was performed, and the resected samples were sent for histopathological examination. The patient showed clinical improvement and was discharged for outpatient follow-up.
One month later, he returned to the hospital with a surgical wound infection. An abdominal CT scan showed diffuse parietal thickening of the small bowel loops, mild distension without obstructive factors, and diffuse densification of the peritoneal layers (Figure 1A). At this time, histopathology from the first surgery revealed a necrotizing granulomatous inflammatory process, a transmural ulcer with hyphae suggestive of mucormycosis (Figure 1B), fibrino-leukocytic peritonitis, acute purulent periappendicitis, reactive lymphoid hyperplasia, and chronic epiploitis with suppuration foci. Mucormycosis was subsequently confirmed by PCR on the paraffin-embedded tissue sample from the total colectomy (Figure 1C). The patient was started on liposomal amphotericin B at a 5 mg/kg/day dosage for 7 weeks, followed by oral posaconazole suspension at 400 mg twice per day. Follow-up abdominal CT scans showed complete clinical and radiological resolution after five months of posaconazole therapy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 49-year-old male presenting with acute diffuse abdominal pain, hypotension, and jaundice following floodwater exposure 10 days prior.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Ten days prior to symptom onset, the patient was exposed to floodwater and accidentally ingested contaminated water. He subsequently presented with acute diffuse abdominal pain, severe hypotension, and jaundice, initially suspected to have a perforated hollow viscus. During his ICU admission, he developed acute renal failure requiring hemodialysis and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage requiring mechanical ventilation. After two weeks of hospitalization, he experienced recurrent episodes of massive enterorrhagia requiring 10 units of packed red blood cells, necessitating emergent total colectomy with end ileostomy. One month post-discharge, he re-presented with a surgical wound infection and recurrent abdominal distress.
subjective.past_medical_history: No prior chronic medical illnesses documented. Occupation: marble and tile setter in construction. Epidemiological exposure: direct exposure to floodwaters and ingestion of contaminated water 10 days prior to symptom onset.
subjective.review_of_systems: Reports acute diffuse abdominal pain, recurrent severe lower gastrointestinal bleeding (enterorrhagia), and surgical wound infection symptoms. Home medications: not documented. Allergies: not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Upon initial presentation: acute diffuse abdominal tenderness, marked jaundice, and arterial hypotension. On re-admission: surgical wound infection of the laparotomy site with abdominal discomfort.
objective.routine_investigations: Laboratory investigation revealed acute renal failure requiring hemodialysis, marked jaundice/hyperbilirubinemia, and severe acute blood-loss anemia requiring massive transfusion of 10 units of packed red blood cells.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial abdominal CT: pneumoperitoneum near the gallbladder and extrahepatic bile ducts. Emergent exploratory laparotomy: cholecystectomy performed; no gastroduodenal or hollow viscus perforation found. Total colectomy and histopathology: transmural ulceration, necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with fungal hyphae suggestive of mucormycosis, fibrino-leukocytic peritonitis, acute purulent periappendicitis, reactive lymphoid hyperplasia, and chronic epiploitis. Follow-up abdominal CT (at 1 month): diffuse parietal wall thickening of small bowel loops, mild non-obstructive bowel distension, and diffuse densification of peritoneal folds. Serial follow-up CT scans at 5 months demonstrated complete radiological resolution.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Severe leptospirosis (Weil's disease triad of jaundice, acute renal failure requiring hemodialysis, and pulmonary hemorrhage) confirmed by two consecutive serologic tests: positive ELISA-IgM and microscopic agglutination test (MAT) for serovar Cynopteri (titer 1/800); complicated by life-threatening lower gastrointestinal hemorrhage (enterorrhagia) and secondary opportunistic gastrointestinal mucormycosis (confirmed by histopathology and paraffin-embedded tissue PCR from colectomy specimen).
Plan & Treatment: Intravenous ceftriaxone for 14 days for leptospirosis; emergent total colectomy with terminal ileostomy and massive blood product transfusion (10 units PRBC); invasive mechanical ventilation and hemodialysis. For gastrointestinal mucormycosis: IV liposomal amphotericin B (5 mg/kg/day) for 7 weeks, followed by oral posaconazole suspension (400 mg twice daily) for 5 months.
Outcome: Complete clinical, laboratory, and radiological cure achieved after five months of antifungal therapy.
